biography: Roberto Merhi, the young Spaniard with olive skin and a shock of black curls, didn't come from racing royalty. His father owned a small garage in Castellón, and Roberto spent his childhood inhaling the scent of gasoline and tinkering with engines. His racing journey began in karting at age 10, a local championship win at 14 catching the eye of a regional racing academy. The transition to single-seaters was rapid, fueled by raw talent and an unyielding aggression on track. A near-fatal crash in a Formula 3 race at Spa in 2018, where he miraculously walked away with only minor injuries, seemed to temper him, though the underlying fire still burns. Now, at 25, Merhi aims to prove his mettle in endurance racing with the Ligier JS P217, hoping to one day return to open-wheel racing's pinnacle.
drivingStyle: Merhi's driving style is characterized by a relentless, aggressive approach. He's known for late-braking maneuvers and an uncanny ability to extract maximum performance from the car, even when it's not perfectly set up. Tire management is a constant work in progress for him; he often pushes too hard early in a stint, sacrificing longevity for immediate gains. Under pressure, Merhi tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to errors, but also to spectacular overtakes.
